officialSemantics.rule: TWSE daily stock limit is +/-10% of the opening-auction reference price, then constrained to legal tick prices without exceeding the limit; listed common stocks may have no limit during specified first-five-day initial-listing periods.
officialSemantics.currentRuleSource: TWSE Operating Rules Articles 62-63, current rule page amended 2026-08-06
officialSemantics.exampleSource: TWSE Trading Mechanism Introduction: reference 40.60 -> theoretical up 44.66/down 36.54 -> legal limit-up 44.65 / limit-down 36.55

fixedLegalCounterexamples.derivation: 100.50 is the highest legal 0.50-tick quote <=100.98; 101.00 would exceed +10%.
10.35 is the lowest legal 0.05-tick quote >=10.305; 10.30 would exceed -10%.
TWSE official example fixes limit-up at 44.65; 44.60 is a lower legal tick but abs(return)>=9.8.
TWSE official example fixes limit-down at 36.55; 36.60 is a higher legal tick but abs(return)>=9.8.

requiredCrossTab: direction separated; never pool positive and negative extreme days for outcome inference
next-open gap, open-to-close, D1/D3/D5, MFE/MAE, executable next-day limit/liquidity state

falsification: If proxy-only non-limit rejects have worse or non-executable next-day paths, retain the proxy despite semantic mismatch.
If exact limit-up rows excluded by the proxy are not materially different from matched non-limit extreme rows after controls, exact-state reformulation may add no value.

If exact positive extreme/limit-up rows show stable opportunity loss with acceptable execution/downside while negative extreme rows remain hazardous, only then consider an asymmetric admission reformulation.
Do not infer direction from limit state alone; delayed price discovery, queue/liquidity and event context remain controls.
